findings.text: Wound-wait test record pairs a wound-wait mutex with an integer counter annotated as guarded by that mutex, expressing that the counter is only touched while the mutex is held.

Local trylock test record pairs a local trylock with a guarded counter and is instantiated as per-CPU storage initialized for the lock, supporting local critical sections that bump the per-CPU counter.

Batched firmware request record carries an index, result code, sent flag, firmware pointer, name and buffer pointers, completion, task pointer and device pointer, allowing parallel issued requests to be tracked and waited upon.

Global test configuration aggregates a name, buffer and offset sizes, several boolean mode flags, small integer counts for request total and read index, an upload name, a pointer to an array of batched records, a result integer and a selector for the firmware request routine.

Upload test object links into a list and holds a name, data buffer with size, a cancel flag, an injected error descriptor and a firmware upload handle; the error descriptor itself pairs a program label with an upload error code.
Minimal debug-virtual record holds a single unsigned integer field and is used through a single static instance pointer allocated at init and released at exit.
Default firmware test identity uses name test-firmware.bin, request count four, buffer size one kilobyte, upload limit two kilobytes and upload block size thirty seven chosen to avoid powers of two.

Dynamic-debug test categories define ten disjoint values starting at zero, three short names starting at eleven, eight version levels starting at fourteen and eight letter levels starting at twenty two, each group encoding a distinct class space.

Per-model class wrapper creates a bits word plus a class parameter binding bits, flags name and map, registered as a module callback parameter with owner read-write mode; test message prefixes are fixed short tags for dynamic-debug and firmware modules.

A single global mutex serializes all firmware test configuration and state: config display, every config store, reset, single and async triggers and misc-device reads acquire it, while batched release and config free have locked and unlocked variants.

Double-underscore helpers for boolean, size and small-integer updates plus batched release and config free assume the caller already holds the global mutex, whereas the similarly named wrappers acquire and release it internally.

Per-CPU raw spinlock test shows two equivalent ways to address a remote CPU instance, by value accessor and by pointer accessor, each followed by lock then unlock with no other work inside the critical section.

Local trylock test demonstrates an unconditional local critical section and a conditional trylock section, each incrementing the per-CPU counter only while the corresponding per-CPU lock is held, with an init helper that guards initialization.

Wound-wait tests exercise blocking, interruptible, try and slow acquisition both without a context and with an initialized acquire context that is marked done and finalized afterwards, always updating the guarded counter under the mutex and destroying the mutex at the end.

Debug-virtual test registers an init routine that translates a fixed vmalloc address and a freshly allocated object to physical addresses with logging, failing cleanly on allocation failure, and an exit routine that releases the object.

Dynamic-debug test provides init and exit hooks that emit start, content and completion messages plus a parameter operations pair whose set and get both invoke the shared print routine, with get also formatting a short confirmation.

Firmware test exposes sysfs show and store handlers for overall config, name, counts, sizes, flags and upload selection plus reset and three trigger stores for sync, platform-embedded and async loading, all operating on the global config.

Firmware test provides a misc-device read that copies currently loaded firmware through a buffered helper under lock and an async completion callback that records the delivered firmware and signals completion; file operations bind the read with module ownership.

Configuration moves from uninitialized to initialized with fixed defaults and null request array, remains mutable until batched requests are allocated, can be reset by freeing then reinitializing under lock, and is freed by releasing requests and clearing the name.

Single firmware slot cycles through empty, loading and loaded: triggers release any prior single and batched state, clear the slot, issue a request, then either publish size and succeed or log failure; async variant waits for the callback signal before checking presence.

Platform test temporarily publishes a stack-resident embedded image with a fixed pattern, forces the checked flag true while saving the prior value, validates returned size and content, then restores the flag, releases firmware, unlinks and frees the name on every exit path.

Print exercise always runs categories then levels after an introductory message; categories cover low, mid, high plus ten driver-oriented classes, levels cover seven version and seven letter classes, driven from init and from parameter accesses.
Request count, buffer size and file offset cannot change while the batched array exists; stores reject such attempts with an invalid error and require releasing all firmware first.

Boolean, size and small-integer stores return the full write length on success even if not all input was consumed and an invalid or parse error otherwise; shows format a single decimal value plus newline within a page, with string shows copying under lock.

Upload selection resolves by linear prefix comparison bounded by stored name length and on success aliases the global upload pointer to the found entry name, else fails invalid; enabling sync-direct switches the request routine to its direct variant, disabling restores the normal one.

Overall config display reports device name plus all tunables, rendering absent name or upload name as an empty marker and send-uevent as one of two action labels; name store replaces the old string with a bounded duplicate of the input.

Async trigger waits for completion while still holding the global mutex and frees the duplicated name immediately after submission to stress lifetime handling, so callback progress and name use must not require that mutex or the freed copy.

Several small show handlers read global config fields without acquiring the mutex while writers update them under lock, and upload selection stores a borrowed pointer to list-owned storage that must outlive the config.

Batched release assumes the request count matches the allocated array length, frees optional const buffers before releasing firmware entries, then frees the array itself; string duplication helpers report memory failure distinctly from success length.

Platform trigger mutates a global embedded-firmware list and checked flag without acquiring any lock visible in these fragments, relying on external serialization if concurrent triggers or readers exist.
